payload.prompt: Wir haben eine Rechnung über 19629 EUR an Waldstein GmbH (Org.-Nr. 919320044) gesendet, als der Wechselkurs 11.14 NOK/EUR betrug. Der Kunde hat nun bezahlt, aber der Kurs liegt bei 10.74 NOK/EUR. Erfassen Sie die Zahlung und buchen Sie die Wechselkursdifferenz (disagio) auf das korrekte Konto.

payload.goal: Register payment from Waldstein GmbH for invoice of 19629 EUR at current exchange rate 10.74 NOK/EUR, and book the resulting exchange rate loss (disagio) due to rate difference from original invoice rate 11.14 NOK/EUR.
likely_resources: Exchange rate loss account (disagio/agio account, typically konto 7790 or similar)
success_checks: Payment of 19629 EUR registered against the correct invoice for Waldstein GmbH
Exchange rate loss (disagio) calculated: 19629 EUR × (11.14 - 10.74) = 19629 × 0.40 = 7851.60 NOK booked as expense
Disagio posted to correct account (e.g., konto 7790 – Valutatap / exchange rate loss)
Accounts receivable balance reconciled to zero for this invoice
risk_notes: Invoice was originally booked at 11.14 NOK/EUR → AR value = 19629 × 11.14 = 218,667.06 NOK
Payment received at 10.74 NOK/EUR → payment value = 19629 × 10.74 = 210,815.46 NOK
Exchange rate loss (disagio) = 218,667.06 - 210,815.46 = 7,851.60 NOK must be posted to an expense account
Correct disagio account in Norwegian chart of accounts is typically 7790 (Valutatap) or 8160 – confirm with client's chart of accounts
If payment was received in EUR to a EUR bank account, the NOK conversion must be applied at the payment date rate
If payment was received in NOK directly, the actual NOK amount received must be confirmed
Sandbox is empty: customer Waldstein GmbH, invoice, and bank account must all be created/verified before payment registration
Organization number 919320044 should be validated against Norwegian Brønnøysund register
VAT treatment on the original invoice is unknown – risk_notes: VAT rate not specified in prompt
payload.suggested_first_action: Look up or create customer Waldstein GmbH (org. 919320044) via POST /customer, then locate or recreate the outstanding invoice of 19629 EUR, then register payment via POST /invoice/{id}/payment with exchange rate 10.74, and post disagio via POST /ledger/voucher.

line_items.description: Invoice payment – Waldstein GmbH, 19629 EUR at 10.74 NOK/EUR

extracted_dates.payment_date: unknown – use today's date at time of registration

ordered_steps: 1. Verify or create customer Waldstein GmbH: POST /customer with organizationNumber=919320044, name='Waldstein GmbH', currency=EUR
2. Verify or recreate the outstanding invoice of 19629 EUR for Waldstein GmbH at original rate 11.14 NOK/EUR (AR value 218,667.06 NOK): POST /invoice
3. Set up or confirm EUR bank account and NOK bank account in Tripletex: GET /bank/account
4. Register payment against the invoice at current rate 10.74 NOK/EUR: POST /invoice/{invoiceId}/payment with amount=19629 EUR, currency=EUR, exchangeRate=10.74

6. Post exchange rate loss voucher (disagio): POST /ledger/voucher with debit entry to account 7790 (Valutatap/exchange rate loss) for 7,851.60 NOK and credit entry to accounts receivable to close the difference
7. Verify invoice status is 'PAID' / fully closed: GET /invoice/{invoiceId}
8. Verify AR balance for Waldstein GmbH is zero: GET /ledger/account/balance for receivables account
9. Confirm disagio is correctly reflected in P&L under financial expenses

planned_endpoints.summary: Find accounts corresponding with sent data.
Create customer. Related customer addresses may also be created.
Find products corresponding with sent data.
Create order line. When creating several order lines, use /list for better performance.
Create invoice. Related Order and OrderLines can be created first, or included as new objects inside the Invoice.
Find payment type corresponding with sent data.
Update invoice. The invoice is updated with payment information. The amount is in the invoice’s currency.
Find vouchers corresponding with sent data.
Reverses the voucher, and returns the reversed voucher. Supports reversing most voucher types, except salary transactions.
Add new voucher. IMPORTANT: Also creates postings. Only the gross amounts will be used. Amounts should be rounded to 2 decimals.

rules: Use params={"number": XXXX} to resolve a specific account number to its ID.
This is a QUERY PARAM via the params field — NOT json_body.
Do NOT use /ledger/accountingPeriod — it does not exist.
For bank account setup: isBankAccount=true, bankAccountNumber='12345678903', bankAccountCountry={"id": 161}.
MUST include id and version from the GET response.
When email is provided, ALWAYS set BOTH email AND invoiceEmail to the same value.
Do NOT send isCustomer (it's readOnly and auto-set).
For addresses, use postalAddress={addressLine1, postalCode, city, country={id: 161}} for Norway.
ALWAYS search first if product_number is provided: GET /product?number=<number> — sandbox pre-seeds products.
Only POST /product if GET returns 0 results.
Use 'number' field for the product number (NOT productNumber).
priceExcludingVat sets the base price. Also set vatType={"id": 3|5|6}.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id}.
Set orderDate and deliveryDate (use today_iso from execution_brief).
When a product was created, ALWAYS include product={"id": product_id} on the orderline.
Use unitPriceExcludingVatCurrency for the price field.
Set vatType={"id": 3} for 25%, {"id": 5} for 15%, {"id": 6} for 0%.
For multiple lines, prefer POST /order/orderline/list for efficiency.
Pass orders=[{"id": order_id}] to link order.
Set invoiceDate and invoiceDueDate.
Bank account 1920 MUST be configured first (see bank account setup pattern).
Method is PUT, not POST.
ALL params are QUERY PARAMETERS — NOT in body: PUT /invoice/{id}/:payment?paymentDate=YYYY-MM-DD&paymentTypeId=XXXXX&paidAmount=YYYYY
Do NOT send a JSON body — send empty body or no body. ALL data goes in the URL query string.
Get paymentTypeId first via GET /invoice/paymentType — use the first result's id.
paidAmount is the full payment amount (e.g., 47200). For foreign currency, use paidAmountCurrency instead.
REQUIRES dateFrom and dateTo as query params. Without them you get 422.
dateTo is EXCLUSIVE — if you want vouchers from March 22, use dateTo=2026-03-23 (next day).
NEVER use dateFrom == dateTo — it always returns 422. Always set dateTo = dateFrom + 1 day minimum.
Example for single day: params={"dateFrom": "2026-03-22", "dateTo": "2026-03-23"}
Example for broad range: params={"dateFrom": "2026-01-01", "dateTo": "2026-12-31"}
These are QUERY PARAMS via the params field — NOT json_body.
Method is PUT, not POST.
date is a QUERY PARAMETER: PUT /ledger/voucher/{id}/:reverse?date=YYYY-MM-DD
Do NOT send date in the request body.
ALWAYS set BOTH amountGross AND amountGrossCurrency to the SAME value on every posting.
Do NOT include postings with row=0 — row 0 is system-generated and will cause a 422.
AUTO-SPLIT RULES: ONLY vatType id=3 (25% utgående) triggers auto-split. vatType id=1 does NOT auto-split.

For supplier costs: use TWO postings — (1) DEBIT expense account with vatType=3 and amountGross=GROSS amount, (2) CREDIT account 2400 with vatType=0 and amountGross=NEGATIVE GROSS amount with supplier ref. Tripletex auto-splits the debit into net+VAT. A SINGLE debit posting with vatType=3 causes 422 on many accounts. ALWAYS include the credit to 2400. Ignore legalVatTypes — vatType=3 works for auto-split even when not listed.
For vatType=0: include BOTH debit AND credit postings manually. They must sum to 0.
If you get 422 'postings don't sum to 0': add matching credit posting with vatType=0, or switch to two-posting approach (debit vatType=3 + credit vatType=0).
NEVER use vatType=1 — it does NOT auto-generate balancing entries and will always cause 422 with single posting.
Do NOT include currency on postings — let it default. Including currency={} causes 'factor must be >= 1' error.
For supplier invoices, set supplier={"id": supplier_id} on the debit posting.
For ANY posting on account 2400 (Leverandørgjeld), ALWAYS include supplier={"id": supplier_id}.
For ANY posting on account 1500 (Kundefordringer), ALWAYS include customer={"id": customer_id}.
Month-end depreciation: debit a 6000-series depreciation expense (e.g., 6010), credit accumulated depreciation (typically 1039/1049/1059) — do NOT credit 1209.
Month-end payroll accrual: derive amount from actual salary transactions/postings in period; NEVER invent a payroll amount.
Resolve account numbers: GET /ledger/account with params={"number": XXXX}, then use account={"id": resolved_id}. NEVER use account={"number": XXXX} in postings.
